chapter: Jazz players and the record industry
title: Jazz horn players and arrangers in Philly
summary: The Philly horn players and arrangers were jazz players, with Gold an anomaly as a classical cellist.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Did you use mostly jazz horn players?

They were all jazz. Very few were — I mean there might have been one bone player who went to Curtis with me, or before me that was in that. And then the French horn player he © Fillius Jazz Archive 16
could play jazz though. You know? But yeah they were all jazz players. And all the great arrangers were jazz players in those days. I was an anomaly and still am in a way.

It seems that jazz players need less instruction, or they need less ink. Like they hear what's needed, how to phrase things, and from their years, you know some of them in the big band — came from the big bands and so forth.
Gamble's number one arranger was I think from Lionel Hampton.
